text:
maya: hey team! opened my first PR (small runtime tweak) and ran into a couple of 1) pre-commit failures on my machine and 2) flaky unit tests in CI. quick pointers?
devon: welcome! for pre-commit we pin versions in `tools/pre-commit-config.yaml`. run `pipx run pre-commit install` or `pre-commit run --all-files` after pulling. If formatting still changes, run `./scripts/format-all` (it runs both black and rustfmt where applicable).
maya: thanks. pre-commit complains about `pyproject.toml` not found when I run inside VSCode integrated terminal. others see that?
devon: VSCode sometimes sets cwd to repo/subdir. Make sure the workspace root points to the repo root or run from repo root. We also added a devcontainer you can `Remote-Containers: Reopen in Container` which sets everything up.
ci-bot: build: failed on tests/unit/test_storage.py::test_db_cleanup - sqlite3.OperationalError: unable to open database file
ryan: that CI failure is usually because the test uses a relative DB path and the runner's workspace is read-only for that step. Locally reproduce with `TEST_DB=$(mktemp)` or `make test-local TEST_FILTER=storage`
maya: i see a note in CONTRIBUTING about 'small PRs vs feature branches' but not sure when to rebase vs merge. What do reviewers expect?
devon: short answer: rebase for tiny bugfixes or doc updates; for multi-commit features leave history intact and we prefer a squash merge on landing. If you prefer to rebase before merge it's fine but don't force-push after review starts unless requested.
maya: awesome. also, branch names? our infra tooling enforces a pattern right?
dryan: branch naming convention: `team/ISSUE-123-short-desc` for cross-team work, `fix/` `feat/` for quicker tweaks. CI auto-triggers coverage and size checks based on branch prefix.
maya: CI showed a coverage dip but local tests passed. ci-bot shows `coverage-diff: -2.4% in inference/core.py`
ci-bot: "coverage-diff check failed: added lines decrease coverage by 2.4% (threshold 1.5%)"
dryan: that one happens if you add new code paths without tests. Add a focused unit test for the new branch in `tests/unit/test_core.py`. If it's a legitimate coverage drop for generated files, add an exclusion in `pytest.ini` scoped to generated artifacts and mention in PR.
maya: one more: my PR changes touches runtime caching; who should I tag for review?
devon: runtime changes: tag @ryan and @sre-leads, add label `triage/runtime` and add a short perf note in the PR template describing expected perf impact and how you tested locally.
maya: thanks. any CI gotchas re: flaky tests?
dryan: yeah, integration tests that need GPU are skipped locally unless you set `CI_RUNTIME_GPU=1`. Also some tests depend on `REDWOOD_CACHE_DIR` env to be writable. Use `make dev-shell` which sets recommended envs. If a test is flaky, mark it with `@flaky` and open a short issue for triage—don't hide flakes in PRs.
devon: extra tip: run `./scripts/ci-sanity.sh` before pushing. It runs lints, unit subset, and size checks so you catch common failures.
maya: sounds good. i fixed the formatting and added a unit for the new branch. pushing now.
ci-bot: pre-commit: passed
ci-bot: unit-tests: running
ci-bot: unit-tests: passed
ci-bot: coverage-diff: passed
ci-bot: size-check: passed
maya: woo! thanks for the pointers everyone — will request review from @ryan and add the triage/runtime label. :party_parrot:
